leaders.name: Steve Daly
leaders.title: Chief Executive Officer
leaders.bio: Steve is a global technology leader guiding Instructure through one of the most transformative eras in education. As CEO, he is leading the company’s shift from an industry-leading LMS provider to a future-ready learning ecosystem that helps institutions and learners navigate rapid technological and workforce change. With more than 25 years of experience scaling global technology companies, Steve is driving Instructure’s expansion across Europe, the Middle East, Asia Pacific, and Latin America, ensuring solutions remain relevant to regional needs while supporting a unified global vision. Since joining Instructure in 2020, Steve has strengthened the company’s foundation and expanded its ecosystem, including Canvas, Mastery, and Parchment, to support learning, assessment, and verified credentials from early education through career development. He frequently emphasizes that the pace of change will not slow down and works with districts, universities, and organizations to build the readiness needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving environment. Before Instructure, Steve held leadership roles at Ivanti, Avocent, and Intel. He holds a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering and an MBA from BYU.

leaders.name: Matt Kaminer
leaders.title: Chief People & Legal Officer
leaders.bio: Matt is the chief people, legal, and administrative officer at Instructure, where he helps guide the company through transformation with clarity, trust, and strong governance. He leads Instructure’s legal, privacy, compliance, and corporate development functions and plays a central role in building a culture that supports growth, accountability, and long-term readiness in a rapidly changing world. Since joining Instructure in 2015, Matt has been a steady leader through pivotal moments, including two IPOs, two private equity transactions, and multiple strategic acquisitions, most recently Parchment. Across each phase of change, he has emphasized thoughtful risk management, people-centered decision making, and responsible innovation. Matt is widely respected for his ability to clarify complex legal, regulatory, and organizational challenges, particularly in areas such as privacy, data protection, and governance. Before Instructure, he held senior legal roles at Collective Inc., Epocrates Inc., MediMedia USA Inc., and WebMD Health Corp. He holds a bachelor’s degree in computer science from Penn State and a J.D. from George Washington University.

leaders.name: Audrey Zhao
leaders.title: Chief Financial Officer
leaders.bio: Audrey is the chief financial officer at Instructure, where she leads the company’s global finance organization and helps ensure the financial strength and operational readiness needed to support a future-ready education technology ecosystem. As Instructure expands its impact across K–12, higher education, and the workforce, Audrey aligns long-term strategy with sustainable growth, enabling confident investment in innovation that enhances human potential and helps learners and educators thrive in a rapidly changing world. Audrey has spent her career scaling technology organizations through periods of rapid growth, transformation, and global expansion. Prior to joining Instructure, she served as CFO at CloudBees, where she helped secure Series F financing that elevated the company to unicorn status and aligned its financial profile with the Rule of 40. Previously, she was senior vice president of finance at Cloudera, guiding the company from startup through the IPO, merger, and acquisition stages. Known for her strategic rigor and steady leadership, Audrey is a trusted partner to boards, CEOs, and teams. She holds degrees from the University of Rochester, Stanford University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

leaders.name: Armin Molavi
leaders.title: President, GCO
leaders.bio: Armin is the chief marketing officer at Instructure. He oversees the company’s brand and go-to-market strategy, advancing a bold, future-focused vision for education technology that enhances human potential and supports educators and learners in a constantly changing environment. His work reflects Instructure’s continued evolution into a global education technology ecosystem that empowers individuals and helps them thrive. Central to Armin’s leadership is a human-centered view of technology. He believes technology should enhance, accelerate, and elevate human capability rather than replace it. This philosophy has guided the evolution of Instructure’s open and interoperable ecosystem, designed to enable mobility and opportunity across every stage of learning, from early education through lifelong and workforce learning. Before joining Instructure, Armin led complex brand-building and growth initiatives across financial services, telecom, retail, CPG, travel, and hospitality, advising global brands including Fidelity, American Express, AT&T, Comcast Xfinity, Procter & Gamble, and Hilton. He has served as an adjunct professor at Brandeis University and is an advisory board member for Harvard University’s Extension School within the Division of Continuing Education. Armin holds a BBA in Marketing from the University of Massachusetts Amherst and lives in Boston with his family.

leaders.name: Shiren Vijiasingam
leaders.title: Chief Product Officer
leaders.bio: Shiren is the chief product officer at Instructure, where he leads the company’s product strategy across learning, assessment, and credentialing. A veteran edtech product leader, Shiren brings decades of experience building data-driven, learner-centric technologies that help educators simplify complexity, align to measurable outcomes, and prepare for rapid technological change. Central to Shiren’s approach is a belief that technology—and especially AI—should serve instructional goals and strengthen, not replace, human relationships in learning. Under his leadership, Instructure has deepened its commitment to openness, delivering an extensible, interoperable platform that gives institutions choice, flexibility, and control while supporting equitable access and learner agency. Before joining Instructure, Shiren served as chief product officer at Newsela and General Assembly, where he launched new product lines, drove significant growth, and helped scale digital learning during periods of rapid change. He has also held senior product leadership roles at WW (formerly Weight Watchers) and The College Board. Based in the New York City metro area, Shiren continues to champion responsible AI and products that expand opportunity and support lifelong learning.

leaders.name: Rachel Orston
leaders.title: Chief Customer Officer
leaders.bio: Rachel is a customer experience leader and transformation strategist who leads institutions through complexity with clarity, confidence, and measurable impact. As chief customer officer at Instructure, she leads global customer success, support, services, and experience strategy, ensuring that educators and learners can fully realize the value of a future-ready ecosystem designed to help people thrive in a rapidly changing world. Rachel’s philosophy centers on readiness, which she defines as the ability for institutions and educators to adapt, respond, and grow amid shifting technologies and evolving learner needs. She champions human-centered innovation and believes technology should work for education by elevating human judgment, strengthening connections, and returning valuable time to educators. A committed mentor and advocate for women in leadership, Rachel empowers emerging leaders to build confidence, resilience, and influence. Before joining Instructure, she served as chief customer officer at SmartRecruiters and BetterCloud and has built customer experience functions across several high-growth SaaS companies. Rachel holds an MBA from Georgia Tech and a Bachelor of Science in Journalism from Northwestern University. As a parent of two long-time Canvas learners, she brings a personal commitment to improving the educational experience for every family and every learner.

leaders.name: Melissa Loble
leaders.title: Chief Learning Officer
leaders.bio: Melissa is a globally recognized education futurist and the chief academic officer at Instructure, where she helps educators and institutions future-proof learning. With more than 25 years of experience across K–12, higher education, nonprofit leadership, and edtech, she brings a unique perspective on how learning must evolve in a rapidly changing world. At Instructure, Melissa guides institutions in translating strategic goals into actionable plans that support lifelong learning and readiness. She chairs the 1EdTech board of directors and serves on the CSU AI Workforce Acceleration Board, advancing global efforts in interoperability, digital ecosystems, and AI-enabled workforce preparation. Melissa began her career as a K-12 educator and has over 20 years of experience in Higher education. She is currently an instructor at the University of California, Irvine, and holds several advisory roles at organizations such as Internet2, Terracotta, and Utah Valley University.

leaders.name: James Sutton
leaders.title: Chief Growth Officer
leaders.bio: James is the chief growth officer at Instructure, where he leads the company’s global growth strategy across revenue, go-to-market execution, and customer expansion. In this role, he plays a central part in advancing Instructure’s evolution into a future-ready education technology ecosystem and positioning the company as a long-term partner for institutions and organizations navigating change across education and the workforce. As learning models evolve and the boundaries between education and work continue to blur, James helps organizations adapt to new expectations around skills, credentials, and lifelong learning. He focuses on aligning growth strategy with the needs of today’s diverse learners, from early education through higher education and into workforce development, ensuring institutions have the clarity, confidence, and support needed to help learners thrive. Prior to joining Instructure, James led global revenue teams at AvidXchange and held senior growth and go-to-market roles at Google, Salesforce, Gusto, and InVision. He holds an MBA from the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management and completed graduate study at Duke University’s Fuqua School of Business.

leaders.name: Brian Cully
leaders.title: SVP, Finance & Strategy
leaders.bio: Brian Cully is a senior vice president of finance and strategy at Instructure, where he leads financial planning, performance insights, and corporate development. In this role, he connects market dynamics to execution, helping shape Instructure’s approach to shifts in education, workforce alignment, and economic mobility while translating complexity into clear, actionable decisions that drive measurable outcomes. Brian plays a central role in aligning business strategy with financial performance. He leads planning, forecasting, and executive and board reporting, providing insight across products and regions to support informed decision-making and sustainable growth. He also oversees corporate development, guiding acquisitions and integration to strengthen Instructure’s position as a partner to institutions worldwide. Known for his ability to connect the dots across a fragmented edtech landscape, Brian translates learner demand shifts, credential models, and workforce needs into financial and strategic decisions. He holds a master’s degree from The Ohio State University and is a CFA charterholder.

leaders.name: Sidharth Oberoi
leaders.title: VP of Global Strategy
leaders.bio: Sidharth is the vice president of partnerships and business development at Instructure, where he helps bring the company’s bold, future focused vision to life through global strategy, collaboration, and execution. With more than seven years at Instructure and over a decade in education technology, he serves as a key connector between innovation, equity, and real world impact across international markets. Sidharth focuses on bridging global divides and connecting learners to economic opportunity regardless of geography. His work helps institutions move beyond tactical readiness toward becoming long term partners in a unified, evidence based education ecosystem that supports learners across every stage of their journey. Previously, Sidharth served as vice president of international strategy, overseeing the global product vision for Canvas and the broader Instructure Learning Platform across APAC, EMEA, and LATAM. He is a frequent speaker and media contributor on global education, skills recognition, and AI. Sidharth serves as a board member for IMS Global Learning Consortium in Europe. He holds a bachelor’s degree from the University of Utah and studied at the University of Washington.

faq.question: How do I reset my password?
faq.answer: If you set up your own Canvas account, go to "Login" and click on the "Forgot Password?" link. Enter the login information associated with your Canvas account and click the "Request Password" button. You'll be sent an email prompting you to reset your password. Once you’ve reset your password, return to the login screen to sign in. For more information, view login tips for: Instructors (opens in a new tab) Students (opens in a new tab) Parents (observers) (opens in a new tab)

faq.question: How do I find my school login?
faq.answer: If you're using Canvas as part of an institution account, you'll log in either from your institution's web page or by using its direct Canvas url. Canvas Network (opens in a new tab) accounts also log in with a Canvas url. Find step-by-step guidance here (opens in a new tab) . Note: You must have an account to log in to Canvas. If you're associated with an institution using Canvas and don't know your username and password, please contact your site administrator. If you're given a join code or a secret url to join a course, learn how to create a Canvas account (opens in a new tab) .

faq.question: As a parent, how do I get an account and log in?
faq.answer: Parents can sign up as an "observer" in Canvas. Observers can link their Canvas account to their student's account so they can see assignment dues dates, announcements, and other course content. In order to create a Canvas account, you'll need the Canvas url associated with the institution where your student is enrolled. If you don't know your institution's Canvas url, contact the institution. If you already have an account from your student's institution, log in to Canvas using the credentials given to you. Find step-by-step guidance here (opens in a new tab) .

faq.question: Where do I access parent resources?
faq.answer: In the Community, there's an entire section devoted to parent resources (opens in a new tab) for Canvas, with helpful links, a forum to ask questions, and a blog. An educator and community coach has also pulled together this guide (opens in a new tab) , where you’ll find step-by-step guidance on pairing codes, best practices for adding and organizing additional students, how to see student courses and grades, notification alerts, and more.

faq.question: How do I get a pairing code?
faq.answer: To link yourself to a student, you'll need to enter a student-specific pairing code. Students can generate pairing codes from their User Settings. Depending on institution permissions, admins and instructors may also be able to generate pairing codes. For more info, visit our Pairing Code FAQ (opens in a new tab) . Depending on your role, there are two places ways to generate pairing codes: How to generate a pairing code for an observer as a student (opens in a new tab) How to generate a pairing code for an observer as an instructor (opens in a new tab)

faq.question: My pairing code is invalid. What should I do?
faq.answer: A few options to consider with an invalid pairing code: If the pairing code has been used by another observer (parent), you'll need a new code. If the pairing code was generated more than seven days ago, you'll need a new code. The pairing code needs to be entered exactly as it displays (they are case sensitive), without spaces. The pairing code needs to be entered from the same institution (i.e. Canvas url) where your student is enrolled. If these troubleshooting tips don't apply, please use the "Report a Problem" option from the app (opens in a new tab) or your browser (opens in a new tab) so we can identify the issue. Please provide the student's email, not your personal email, as it's not accessible in our system.

faq.question: What can I do with a Free Account?
faq.answer: As an Instructor, you can create courses, add students, build or pull content to deliver curriculum, and more. As a Student, you can access your coursework, communicate and collaborate with other students, and view grades on desktop or mobile. Parents can be added as an observer, too!

faq.question: I need help with my Free Canvas Account. Where should I go?
faq.answer: For help with your Free for Teacher account, check out our Free for Teacher Account FAQ (opens in a new tab) in the Canvas Community.

faq.question: Can I use it even though I'm not a teacher?
faq.answer: Yes! Students, their parents, and anyone else who wants to use Canvas learning tools can sign up.

faq.question: What are the limitations?
faq.answer: The Free Canvas Accounts don't contain all the features available to institutional users of Canvas. Check out this Canvas Account Comparison (opens in a new tab) guide to see the difference.

faq.question: How do I get a join code?
faq.answer: If you're using Canvas through your institution, you will most likely already have an account and need to accept a course invitation. Your institution will email your login information. If you do not yet have an account, you can create an account when you accept the course invitation. If you're not using Canvas through your institution, you can create your own account. Your instructor will provide you with a join code to link you directly to the course. This code will be sent to you separately from the Canvas email that invites you to join the course. If you need to create an account in Canvas but haven't received your join code via email, please contact your instructor or institution for help with logging in. Follow this step-by-step guidance (opens in a new tab) .

faq.question: As a current customer, where should I go for help?
faq.answer: Visit your Canvas Dashboard and click on the “Help” button at the bottom of the Global Navigation. From there, you’ll be able to access a range of helpful resources and The Training Services Portal. You can also reach out to your school's admin for support or visit the resource guides and forums in the Community (opens in a new tab) .

faq.question: Where do I find the Canvas Help Button?
faq.answer: Visit your Canvas Dashboard and click on the “Help” button at the bottom of the Global Navigation. From there, you’ll be able to access a range of helpful resources and The Training Services Portal.

faq.question: What do I do if I can’t access my account?
faq.answer: If you can't log in to Canvas, follow this step-by-step guidance (opens in a new tab) . If you're trying to log into a Free for Teacher account, visit this guide (opens in a new tab) .

faq.question: Where can I find free Canvas courses?
faq.answer: The Canvas Network (opens in a new tab) offers open, online courses from experts and institutions worldwide. If you need training on Canvas, free Canvas training courses can be found here (opens in a new tab) .
